Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: [INCIDENT] p95 spike on gen-api for finmate-prod (initial alert)

Quick heads-up: monitoring alerted at 09:08 PST for an ongoing p50/p95 increase on the gen-api serving pool pinned to finmate-prod. Observed behavior:
- p50 increased from ~60ms to ~240ms across requests with average seq_len=256
- p95 climbed to ~1.8s for a 10-minute window, throughput down ~22%
- error rate (500s) up from 0.02% to 0.6% during the same window

I've captured a Grafana snapshot and started a short bucketed trace (link below). Initial hypothesis: slow kernel path on a subset of GPUs combined with KV cache misses due to a change in request distribution after 08:55 PST. No customer-facing outage escalations yet but FinMate calls began showing increased timeouts at ~09:05.

Immediate actions taken:
- throttled non-critical background batch jobs on the cluster
- pinned new requests to fallback variant (gen-api-v1.3-q4) for affected tenant routing
- spun up two additional small instances in us-west to absorb burst

Next steps I recommend: full traffic fallback to v1.3-q4 for FinMate (15–30m) while we collect traces and decide on kernel rollback vs. quantization runtime switch. Need product and CS language for a short customer note.

Grafana: https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/ops/finmate-genapi?orgId=1&panelId=7 (snapshot attached: grafana-snapshot.png)

--
Marissa
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: [INCIDENT] p95 spike on gen-api for finmate-prod (initial alert)

Thanks for the quick triage, Marissa. A few clarifying Qs before we finalize customer comms:
1) Scope: which endpoints are returning 500s? Are these primarily streaming or non-streaming generate calls?
2) Rollback cost: if we route FinMate to v1.3-q4, what CPU/GPU delta do we expect and will that materially affect other tenants?
3) ETA: how long to confirm kernel rollback vs runtime-quantization switch?

Dylan, can you prioritize a kernel health check and confirm whether the slow path is (a) an attention kernel regression or (b) memory-path fragmentation on the effected GPU group? If (a) we should prepare a rollback. If (b) a cache warming plus eviction policy tweak might be faster.

Vivek/Stephanie — please draft a customer note that we can send once we agree on the short fallback and expected ETA. Keep it concise, mention we're routing to a compatible variant to maintain availability and that we'll follow up with a timeline and postmortem.

I'll stand by on gating a rollback — need your readouts first.

-karthik
Head of Product, Serving Runtime

Subject: DRAFT: customer note for FinMate — brief status and short fallback

Draft below — please edit for technical accuracy. My aim is to be transparent, brief, and set expectations.

Subject: Brief service note — temporary routing change to preserve availability

Hi Lila,

We wanted to let you know we observed elevated latency and a small increase in timeouts for FinMate requests in the us-west region this morning. To preserve availability while our SRE team completes a targeted investigation, we've routed your traffic to a compatible inference variant that maintains the same model behavior but uses a different runtime path. This change should reduce timeouts immediately; we do not expect changes to model outputs.

What we're doing now:
- Redirecting live traffic to a fallback runtime variant (15–30 minute window while we validate)
- Collecting traces and logs to determine whether a kernel rollback or runtime tweak is required
- Preparing a post-incident summary and actionable plan once root cause is confirmed

What to expect:
- Immediate reduction in observed timeouts; minor latency differences possible (<250ms typical)
- We'll follow up within 2 hours with an ETA for full resolution and a timeline for a postmortem

If you prefer we can keep you on the original path while we fix the underlying issue — let us know and we can coordinate a controlled window.

Apologies for the interruption; we appreciate your patience.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

--
